responsibilities.name: Infrastructure Health Check
responsibilities.instruction: Run infrastructure health check — verify all managed services are running, check disk usage, review recent error logs, and alert if anything needs attention.

context.purpose: Proactive infrastructure monitoring. Catch issues before they become outages. DevOps agents manage GCP VMs, Firebase projects, and deployed services — all need regular health verification.
process: Check VM disk usage — alert if any disk is above 80% capacity
Verify all systemd services are running (agent-ears, agent-mouth, agent-brain, openclaw-gateway)
Review the last 50 lines of each service log for ERROR or FATAL entries
Check Docker container health (openclaw-gateway status, restart count)
Verify Firestore connectivity by reading a known document
Check memory/CPU usage — alert if sustained above 80%
If any issues found, attempt auto-remediation (restart service, clear cache) before alerting
context.success_criteria: All services verified running. Disk/memory/CPU within thresholds. Any issues auto-remediated or escalated with specific details.
context.prior_learnings: The most common issue is disk usage from accumulated Docker images and log files. 'docker system prune -f' and log rotation usually resolves disk pressure. Gateway restart requires 'sudo systemctl restart openclaw-gateway' on the host, not inside Docker.

responsibilities.name: Daily Deployment Verification
responsibilities.instruction: Verify all active deployments are serving correctly. Check Firebase Hosting preview URLs, Cloud Run services, and any project-specific endpoints.

context.purpose: Deployments can silently break due to SSL cert expiry, DNS changes, or Firebase project config drift. Daily verification catches these before users report them.
process: List all known deployed URLs from memory and workspace notes
For each URL, perform an HTTP GET and verify status 200
Check SSL certificate expiry — alert if less than 14 days remaining
Verify Firebase Hosting channel deployments are still active (channels can expire)
Check Cloud Run service health endpoints if applicable
Report: total URLs checked, any failures with specific error details
context.success_criteria: All known deployments verified accessible. Any failures reported with URL, status code, and error details.
context.prior_learnings: Firebase preview channels have a default 7-day expiry. If a preview URL returns 404, it likely expired and needs redeployment. Use 'firebase hosting:channel:deploy <channel> --project <project>' to redeploy. Always specify --project explicitly.
